title: Universal Definition of Mental Disorder and Mental Disability Across All Legislation
what_it_is: Universal Definition of Mental Disorder and Mental Disability Across All Legislation

sections.label: Common definition of mental disorder
sections.summary: The Government is open to a common, universal definition of mental disorder and mental disability if it meets policy intent across legislation, with safeguards in the criminal justice system.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: There is some variation in the way that mental conditions are treated.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: However, the Government is open to suggestions for a common, universal definition of mental disorder and mental disability if such a definition can meet the policy intent across all the different pieces of legislation.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Safeguards are built in for persons with mental health conditions in the criminal justice system.

sections.label: Mandatory Treatment Order and prison treatment
sections.summary: Courts can impose a Mandatory Treatment Order for psychiatric treatment instead of imprisonment, and inmates with mental health needs have access to treatment in prison.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: In appropriate cases, the Court can impose a Mandatory Treatment Order for the offender to undergo psychiatric treatment, instead of sentencing him to imprisonment.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: In prison, inmates with mental health needs have access to the necessary treatment for their condition.

sections.label: Reviews and common mental health standard
sections.summary: Reviews occur from time to time but should not constrain suggestions, and a common standard across differing policy intents would be welcomed and considered.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I was wondering whether there are any reviews upcoming and whether the Interagency Taskforce for Mental Health and Well-being can look into this to figure out a common meaning and understanding for future legislation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: We do review from time to time but do not let the fact that there is or is not a review constrain any suggestions that you might have to give to us.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Certainly, as I have said earlier with my illustrations, there are some nuances to be looked at and to be appreciated in the contexts of the different standards and the different contextual circumstances in which mental disability or treatment, or even mental capacity, might arise, and how they are defined in the context of certain pieces of legislation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Some seek to diminish responsibility, others seek to deal with the questions of whether you can appropriately consent and yet others deal with the question of whether we should appropriately protect the person with disability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: So, if we can find a common standard across the spectrum that deals with all these various policy intents and purposes, then, of course, we welcome the Member to propose a definition to us and we will consider it.
